sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-full/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 15 (check 14) and Internal Quality Checks row 15 annotation ('If task data itself contain credential falg it. Only in toml we allow.')
evidence: The only shipped data asset, task/environment/assets/seed_data.json (149 bytes, sha256 30cf9958eca69569e0c78ca3ce4ec239c167dd41342baa361c10355b3d92e4b8), parses and contains only {"snippets": [], "note": "No saved snippets are supplied in this seed. Build a JavaScript and HTML playground with durable revision history."}; with zero records there are no ids that can dangle, and it agrees with instruction.md:3 and integration.md:7 ('contains no user snippets or starter implementation'). All other shipped JSON (solution/app/package.json, tsconfig.json, package-lock.json) parses and holds only package metadata; a regex sweep of environment/, instruction.md, solution/app/src, server.js and tests prompts found no emails, phone numbers, API keys or prompt-injection phrases, the sole address being the reserved 'turing@local.invalid' git identity in environment/Dockerfile:20. The solution server.js never imports the seed and builds the snippets/revisions schema empty, and tests/app_context.md:26 tells the judge not to assume an empty library, so no criterion depends on a seeded figure; the empty 'snippets' list is internally consistent with the template's CHANGE_ME placeholder having been replaced. Counterexample probe: a broken app cannot gain from the seed (nothing to copy), and a conforming app that ignores the seed loses nothing, so the seed neither pre-satisfies nor misleads grading.
